rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The repeated warning addresses two resurrection scenes: honor when the righteous see their abode, then exposure when the wicked see theirs.
rows.anchor: أنه كرر ذلك لأنه في موقفين، موقف الإكرام، وموقف الفضيحة، وذلك جميعا في الحشر

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The repetition intensifies the warning and threat.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كرر تأكيدا ووعيدا، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The first warning comes at despair and the second at resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كلا سوف تعلمون عند اليأس، ثم كلا سوف تعلمون في الحشر، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Kalla is a rebuke and restraint; another view takes it as emphasis in a threat, as Arabs also emphasize with haqqan.
rows.anchor: كلا قيل: ردع وزجر، وقيل: تأكيد في الوعيد، والعرب تؤكد ب (كلا) و (حقا)

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrase may be an oath meaning if only you knew with certain knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو قسم لو تعلمون علم اليقين أي: علما يقينا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Certainty and knowledge are synonymous terms joined because their wording differs; alternatively the phrase means certain knowledge, like haqq al-yaqin.
rows.anchor: واليقين والعلم واحد، فأضاف أحدهما إلى الآخر لاختلاف اللفظين، وقيل: معناه العلم اليقين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Knowledge may be necessary or acquired; acquired knowledge of the Resurrection becomes certainty when joined to necessary knowledge, then becomes direct observation.
rows.anchor: العلم يكون بمسانيد، وضرورة، ويكون باكتساب، وإذا انضاف الضروري إلى المكتسب صار يقينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will see Hell at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: [لترون الجحيم] يعني: في القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will see Hell with direct sight when they enter it and are punished there.
rows.anchor: [ثم لترونها عين اليقين] بالمشاهدة إذا دخلوها وعذبوا بها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The three occurrences of kalla mark knowledge at death, in the grave, and at the gathering; the final knowledge is certain because it is witnessed.
rows.anchor: ذكر (كلا) ثلاث مرات أي: ستعلمون عند اليأس، وفي القبر، وفي الحشر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The questioned blessing encompasses every religious and worldly kind and asks how people used it and whether they gave thanks; it is a rebuke.
rows.anchor: عن جميع أجناس النعم دينا ودنيا كيف صنعتم فيها، وهل شكرتم أم لا، وكل ذلك سؤال توبيخ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Sound senses, pleasant tastes, a healthy self, and cold water are examples within the general blessings already mentioned.
rows.anchor: الحواس السليمة، والأذواق الطيبة، والنفس الصحيحة، والماء البارد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The question concerns every pleasure of worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: [عن] كل لذة من لذات الدنيا، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: People will be asked how they acted upon the Qur'an and Islamic laws.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القرآن وشرائع الإسلام كيف [عملتم] بها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet names a sheltering house, covering garment, and morsel of food as blessings, along with everything beyond them.
rows.anchor: بيت يؤويك، وخرقة تواري عورتك، وكسرة تشد بها صلبك وما سوى ذلك من النعيم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a reported reading of the surah, hoarding wealth means collecting it unlawfully, withholding its due, and storing it; the graves are entered, and the reckoning follows at the gathering.
rows.anchor: تكاثر الأموال جمعها من غير حقها، ومنعها عن حقها، وشدها في الأوعية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The report places sight of Hell at the crossing of the bridge over Hell and lists five blessings to be questioned: satiety, cold drink, sleep, shade, and sound constitution.
rows.anchor: عن خمس: شبع البطون، وبارد الشراب، ولذة النوم، وظلال المساكن، واعتدال الخلق

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The blessings include health, free time, and wealth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الصحة والفراغ والمال، عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، ومجاهد
rows.claim: The blessings are security and health.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأمن والصحة، عن ابن مسعود، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The blessings are food, drink, and all other pleasures.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المأكل والمشرب وسائر الملاذ، عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: The blessing is well-being.
rows.anchor: وقيل: العافية، عن علي

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: The blessing is God's favor to people through Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عما أنعم عليكم بمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، عن محمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and has five verses.
rows.anchor: مكية فيما روي، وهي خمس آيات

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Ubayy promises that recitation protects a person during life from slander and metamorphosis.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة (الفيل) عافاه الله أيام حياته في الدنيا من القذف والمسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah confirms the previous warning: God recounts what He did to the Elephant army and how He saved believers after condemning slanderers attached to worldly life.
rows.anchor: بين في هذه السورة ما فعله بأصحاب الفيل، وكيف نجى المؤمنين؛ تأكيدا لما تقدم

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has tarmeehum with feminine ta referring to the birds as a group.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: (ترميهم) بالتاء كناية عن الطير وهي جماعة

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف وأشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: They read with ya, referring the act of throwing to God; another explanation refers it to the noun birds, which lacks a feminine marker, and this reading is also reported from Abu Hanifa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف وأشهب العقيلي بالياء كناية عن ذكر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd means plotting or exertion, sometimes a concealed intent to harm and sometimes simply intention; the commentary illustrates its use with Yusuf and the idols.
rows.anchor: الكيد: الاحتيال والاجتهاد، ومنه سميت الحرب كيدا لاحتيال الناس فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dalal originally means leaving the straight course and can mean blameworthy religious error, inadvertent error, loss, or destruction.
rows.anchor: والضلال: أصله الذهاب عن سبيل القصد، ضل يضل ويضل بكسر الضاد وفتحها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan according to a report and has four verses.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية فيما روي، وهي أربع آيات

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's report promises ten good deeds for every person who circumambulates the Kaaba and performs retreat there.
rows.anchor: أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من طاف بالكعبة، واعتكف بها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Umm Hani's report says Quraysh were favored because the Prophet was among them, prophethood and watering were theirs, they defeated the Elephant army, and worshipped God alone for ten years.
rows.anchor: فضل قريشا لأني منهم، وأن النبوة فيهم، والسقاية فيهم، ونصرهم على الفيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some treated Elephant and Quraysh as one surah because Ubayy's codex had no separation between them.
rows.anchor: إن سورة (الفيل) و(قريش) سورة واحدة، فرووا أن في مصحف أبي لا فصل بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are two surahs, as held by most Companions and Successors and established by the method for determining surah divisions; Umar's recitation of both in one rakah proves no unity.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنهما سورتان، وعليه جل الصحابة والتابعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening recalls Quraysh's blessings, following the previous surah's mention of the blessing of destroying the Elephant army.
rows.anchor: ولما ختم السورة بذكر نعمه على قريش بإهلاك أصحاب الفيل، افتتح هذه السورة يذكر نعمه عليهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far reads li-ilaf without hamza; Ibn Amir reads a lightly articulated hamza with ya for ease; the rest retain the fully lengthened original form.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر: [ليلاف] بغير همز، وقرأ ابن عامر: [لإلاف قريش] مهموزا مختلسا بالياء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, through Ibn Fuleih, reads ilfihim with a quiescent lam; a reading like Abu Ja'far's is also transmitted from him.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير في رواية ابن فليح: (إلفهم) ساكنة اللام

rows.speaker: محمد بن حبيب
rows.claim: A transmission from Asim through Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash has two hamzas, but the author says that report is unsound and prefers Asim's fully lengthened īlāfihim reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذه الرواية غير صحيحة، والصحيح عنه: إيلافهم مشبعة الهمزة بعدها ياء

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads liya'lafa Quraysh ilfihim.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عكرمة: (ليألف قريش إلفهم)

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Ilaf and ilf have the same meaning though their verb forms differ; the explanation distinguishes their conjugations and says the sense is one.
rows.anchor: الإيلاف والإلف بمعنى، قال أبو مسلم: وهذا مما اتفق فيه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited line about camels refusing watering places and becoming accustomed illustrates the verb alifa/ālafa.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: أبت إبلي ماء الحياض وآلفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilf is habitual attachment that settles the soul; alafa makes someone accustomed, with familiar derivatives and inas as its analogue and ihash as its opposite.
rows.anchor: والإلف لزوم الشيء على عادة في سكون النفس إليه، ألف يألف إلفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'lif is a relation joining two parts and belongs to a distinct genus among accidents.
rows.anchor: ومنه التأليف معنى يحل جزءين لا يشاركه في هذا عرض، وبه فارق سائر الأعراض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Rihlah is accusative as a verbal noun for their journeying.
rows.anchor: فقيل: نصب على المصدر، أي: ارتحالهم رحلة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats rihlah as the object of their habituation, understood as their becoming accustomed to a journey.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نصب لوقوع إيلافهم عليهم، تقديره: ليألفوا رحلة، عن الأخفش

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis makes rihlah an adverbial accusative meaning on a journey.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نصب على الظرف بمعنى: على رحلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, rihlah is nominative, with the two journeys supplying its implied subject.
rows.anchor: وقيل: محله رفع على تقدير: هما رحلة الشتاء والصيف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The occasion is described as a seven-year drought in Mecca after the Prophet prayed against Mudar; leaders asked him to pray, and rain and food from Yemen followed before the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: فجدبوا سبع سنين حتى أكلوا الكلاب والجيف والعظام المحرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh means Mecca and the descendants of Nadr ibn Kinana; another definition excludes anyone not descended from Nadr.
rows.anchor: أي: لتأتلف مكة وقريش ولد النضر بن كنانة، وقيل: من لم يلده النضر فليس بقريش

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation derives Quraysh from gathering, since they gathered together.
rows.anchor: فقيل: القريش الجمع، يقال: تقرشوا؛ أي: تجمعوا، فلجمعهم سموا بذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation derives their name from accumulating wealth and trade.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لتكسبهم الأموال وجمعها، وتجاراتهم سموا بذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third explanation names them after a sea creature that overcomes other sea animals; the quoted verse says the creature dwells in the sea and gave Quraysh its name.
rows.anchor: بل قريش دابة في البحر، تغلب سائر ما في البحر من الدواب

rows.speaker: ابن زيد، والكلبي، وجماعة
rows.claim: Quraysh travelled to Syria in summer and Yemen in winter for trade.
rows.anchor: رحلة الصيف إلى الشام، ورحلة الشتاء إلى اليمن في التجارة، عن ابن زيد، والكلبي، وجماعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Another account says they wintered in Mecca and summered in Taif, and were told to remain in the sanctuary and worship its Lord.
rows.anchor: كانوا يشتون بمكة، ويصيفون بالطائف، فأمر الله أن يقيموا بالحرم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: A third account says they travelled from cold regions in winter to warm regions and from hot regions in summer to cool ones.
rows.anchor: كان بالشام أرض باردة وأرض حارة، فكانوا يرحلون في الشتاء إلى الحارة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations say God granted them residence in Mecca and spared them from leaving, or secured them on their two journeys.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه أنعم عليهم بالمقام بمكة، وأغناهم عن الخروج، وقيل: بل أمنهم في أسفارهم في الرحلتين

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The first interpretation asks Quraysh to stay attached to Mecca as they were to the two trades: God made pilgrims and commerce bring goods so they no longer needed travel, while protecting them from enemies.
rows.anchor: لتألف قريش مكة كإلفهم التجارتين فلا يفارقوها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation asks Quraysh to become accustomed to worshipping God as they were to the two journeys.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ليألفوا عبادة الله، كما ألفوا الرحلتين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Their pre-Islamic trips earned their livelihood; after Islam, pilgrimage and goods brought to Mecca made travel unnecessary, and the verse recalls those blessings.
rows.anchor: فلما جاءهم الإسلام، ووجب الحج، واستغنوا عن ذلك، وجلبوا إلى مكة ما أغناهم عن الارتحال

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: God secured them on their journeys because people revered the residents of Mecca as inhabitants of the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: فمن عليهم بأن أمنهم في أسفارهم بما جعل في قلوب الناس من تعظيم أهل مكة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Quraysh should worship the Lord of the House because He made them independent of their two journeys.
rows.anchor: ليعبدوا رب هذا البيت قريش من أجل ما أنعم عليهم من الاستغناء عن الرحلتين

rows.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: The sanctuary was a barren valley and their journeys supplied their livelihood; people left them unharmed as custodians of God's House, then fertility and imported food relieved them of the journeys, so they were ordered to worship.
rows.anchor: وكان لهم رحلتان بهما معاشهم، ولا يتعرض أحد لهم بسوء، يقولون: سكان حرم الله

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: God destroyed the Elephant army to gather and increase Quraysh, preserve their trade and keep them in Mecca so Muhammad could emerge among them; He protected them from Arab attacks and fed them.
rows.anchor: فعل ما ذكره في سورة (الفيل) لتأتلف قريش وتجتمع وتكثر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The lām may be imperative: Quraysh should remain in Mecca and worship the House's Lord as they were accustomed to the journeys.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اللام لام الأمر؛ أي: لتألف قريش بمكة، وليعبدوا رب هذا البيت

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj understands the lām as preserving Quraysh and their familiar two journeys.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لتبق قريش وما ألفوه من الرحلتين، عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they should become attached to the House as they were to the two journeys.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ليألفوا البيت كإلفهم الرحلتين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: God fed them by giving wealth and providing sustenance.
rows.anchor: قيل: ما أعطاهم من الأموال، وسبب لهم من الأرزاق

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: God fed them by inclining pilgrims and others to bring every kind of blessing to Mecca.
rows.anchor: بما أوقع في قلوب الحاج وغيرهم حتى جلبوا إليها كل نعمة، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: God provided causes that brought blessings; after the Abyssinians perished, pilgrimage increased and people brought trade and provisions to Mecca, easing their livelihood.
rows.anchor: لما هلكت الحبشة قويت الدواعي إلى الحج، فقصدوا مكة بأنواع التجارات والنعم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: God secured them from raids through the sanctuary, which God had made Arabs revere.
rows.anchor: أمنهم من خوف الغارة بالحرم الذي جبل قلوب العرب على تعظيمه، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They were safe on journeys because they could declare themselves people of God's sanctuary, whom nobody would attack.
rows.anchor: كانوا إذا قالوا في سفرهم: نحن أهل حرم الله، لا يتعرض لهم أحد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another account attributes their security to their large numbers, strength, and wealth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمنوا بكثرة العدد والقوة والأموال، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: الضحاك، والربيع، وسفيان، وشريك
rows.claim: They were protected from leprosy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمنهم من الجذام، فلا يصيبهم ذلك أبدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations say they were protected from the Abyssinians or that the caliphate would remain among them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمنهم من الحبشة، وقيل: أمنهم من أن تكون الخلافة إلا فيهم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Security means that the caliphate would remain among Quraysh.
rows.anchor: عن علي (عليه السلام)

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other views say God secured them through Abraham's prayer or through the Prophet, Islam, and provision.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمنهم بدعوة إبراهيم، وقيل: أمنهم بالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، والإسلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: For those who are not hypocrites, heedlessness means neglecting prayer with a distracted heart and little regard for it; the show-off is blamed for carelessness, unlike the hypocrite blamed for hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: يغفل عن صلاته، ويقصر فيها، وقلبه مشغول بغيرها، لا يرى لها منزلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومسروق
rows.claim: The heedless delay their prayers beyond their appointed times.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ساهون: يؤخرونها عن وقتها، عن ابن عباس، ومسروق

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Sa'id says he asked the Prophet about the verse and was told it concerns people who delay prayer past its time.
rows.anchor: سألت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن هذه الآية فقال: الذين يؤخرون الصلاة عن وقتها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another view describes people distracted from prayer even while performing it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لاهون عنها مع أدائها، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view describes one who prays only for show and feels no regret when missing prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي إن صلاها صلاها رياء، وإن فاتته لم يندم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says they miss prayer times and fail to complete bowing and prostration; another report from him identifies one who looks around.
rows.anchor: لا يصلونها بمواقيتها، ولا يتمون ركوعها وسجودها، عن أبي العالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blameworthy heedlessness must be the servant's own act rather than God's act, so that the rebuke makes sense.
rows.anchor: والأظهر - بل الواجب - أنه أراد بالسهو ما هو فعل العبد، دون ما هو فعل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse most fittingly addresses hypocrites, since they perform deeds for people to see and the surah opens by describing deniers.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن تحمل الآية على أهل النفاق؛ لأن أول السورة في المكذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although hypocrites' acts are not genuine prayer, the outward form lets the verse call them prayer by extension, as another verse calls their false religion religion.
rows.anchor: لأن صورته صورة الصلاة، فسماه صلاة توسعا

rows.speaker: عطاء بن دينار
rows.claim: The wording says heedless about their prayer rather than heedless within it: the former leaves prayer, while the latter still performs it, which better suits hypocrites.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي قال: (الذين هم عن صلاتهم) ولم يقل: (في صلاتهم)

rows.speaker: علي، وابن عمر، وابن الحنفية، والحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Al-ma'un is the obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: قيل: هي الزكاة الواجبة، عن علي، وابن عمر، وابن الحنفية، والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وابن عمر، وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Al-ma'un is the shared household gear people lend one another, such as an axe, pot, or bucket.
rows.anchor: الماعون: ما يتداوله الناس بينهم من الفأس، والقدر، والدلو

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، وأبو علي
rows.claim: Al-ma'un can mean ordinary household items borrowed by neighbors; Abu Ali says this portrays extreme stinginess and baseness.
rows.anchor: هو ما يسأله الجيران بعضهم من بعض من الأمتعة التي يستعيرها الناس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report repeatedly identifies al-ma'un as zakat and urges people to pay it to be saved; the author prefers this because abandoning zakat merits the threat.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: الماعون الزكاة - أربع مرات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Lending was obligatory at the beginning of Islam because the emigrants were poor, then became permissible as circumstances improved.
rows.anchor: كانت العارية واجبة في ابتداء الإسلام لضيق ذات يد المهاجرين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse condemns their low character because they would not help vulnerable believers.
rows.anchor: ذم هؤلاء لأنهم لخستهم لا يعينون ضعفاء المؤمنين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب، والزهري، ومقاتل
rows.claim: In Qurayshi usage, al-ma'un means wealth.
rows.anchor: الماعون بلسان قريش: المال، عن سعيد بن المسيب، والزهري، ومقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation defines al-ma'un as obedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الطاعة، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب، والكلبي
rows.claim: Another interpretation defines al-ma'un as all good deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو المعروف كله، عن محمد بن كعب، والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the previous surah condemned abandoning prayer and withholding alms, this one promises the Prophet abundant good despite their denial and orders prayer.
rows.anchor: بين في هذه السورة أنهم إن منعوه وكذبوه فالله يعطيه الخير الكثير، وأمره بالصلاة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's report promises drink from the rivers of Paradise and ten good deeds for every sacrifice made on Eid.
rows.anchor: سقاه الله من أنهار الجنة، وأعطاه من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد كل قربان

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makhul's report describes immeasurable heavenly rewards, with innumerable camels and world-sized notebooks recording the reciter's palaces and dwellings in Paradise.
rows.anchor: كل بعير عليه كراريس، كل كراسة مثل الدنيا وما فيها

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has a'ṭaynaka with the letter ʿayn, meaning We gave you.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: (إنا أعطيناك) بالعين من العطاء

rows.speaker: الحسن وطلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Hasan and Talha read anṭaynaka with nun; it is reported from the Prophet and means We gave, replacing ʿayn with nun.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن وطلحة بن مصرف: (أنطيناك) بالنون، وروي ذلك مرفوعا

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi says the Prophet dignified the Himyarite form anṭihi, meaning give it to him; Zayd ibn Thabit reports hearing it while the Prophet dictated a document.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: قد شرف النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - هذه اللغة وهي حميرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving means putting something into a recipient's hands; its root conveys reaching or taking, as in the phrase I gave him and he took it.
rows.anchor: الإعطاء: إخراج الشيء إلى آخذ له، وأصله: التناول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawthar derives on the faw'al pattern from abundance and means abundant gifts or abundant good.
rows.anchor: والكوثر: بناؤه فوعل من الكثرة كنوفل من النفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shani' means hater, while abtar is cut off from good and can describe a childless man, anything with no continuing trace, or a tailless animal; an incomplete sermon is also called batra'.
rows.anchor: والأبتر: المنقطع عن الخير، وأصله الذي انقطع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The surah was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il, who called the Prophet abtar after speaking with him outside the mosque.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه السورة في العاص بن وائل السهمي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt called the Prophet abtar.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في عقبة بن أبي معيط، وهو قال للنبي

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report connects the verse to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Quraysh preferring themselves over Muhammad; the author calls this far-fetched because the episode was after the Hijra and Badr while the surah is Meccan.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد؛ لأن قصة كعب كانت بعد الهجرة، وبعد بدر، وهذه السورة مكية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say Quraysh called the Prophet abtar after his son Abdullah died, using the term for a man without a son.
rows.anchor: توفي لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ابن يسمى عبد الله، فسمته قريش أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They thought his mission would end because he had no male successor; the verse refutes them, declaring their religion cut off while Islam rises each day.
rows.anchor: فيهم نزلت الآية، فكذبهم، وجعل دينهم الأبتر، وأظهر دين الإسلام يزيد كل يوم علوا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: One report places the command to pray and sacrifice at Hudaybiyya when the Prophet and companions were barred from the House; the author rejects this as far-fetched because the surah is Meccan and Hudaybiyya was two years after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزل قوله: (فصل لربك وانحر) يوم الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence means God granted abundant good, so the Prophet should give thanks through prayer and sacrifice and persevere, since God will destroy his enemies.
rows.anchor: إنا أعطيناك الخير الكثير، فصل شكرا، وانحر، واصبر، فإنا نهلك أعداءك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The abundant good includes religious laws calling for prayer and festival sacrifices, as well as the destruction of enemies.
rows.anchor: خيرا كثيرا منها الشرائع ليصلوا وينحروا في الأعياد، ومنها هلاك الأعداء

rows.speaker: عائشة، وابن عمر
rows.claim: Kawthar is a river in Paradise with banks of pearl and ruby; this is attributed to Aisha and Ibn Umar and transmitted from the Prophet, and is Abu Ali's view.
rows.anchor: قيل: نهر في الجنة، حافتاه الدر والياقوت، عن عائشة، وابن عمر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet describes Kawthar as a river whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, with birds whose necks resemble camels' necks and food more pleasant than the birds.
rows.anchor: نهر أعطاني الله تعالى، أشد بياضا من اللبن، وأحلى من العسل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says Kawthar is a river in Paradise whose flowing sound can be heard by putting a finger in one's ear.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة: نهر في الجنة، من أحب أن يسمع خريرها

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies Kawthar as the Prophet's pool where people will gather on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: والذي يكثر الناس عليه يوم القيامة، عن عطاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Kawthar means abundant good; the author prefers this because it encompasses all the more specific interpretations.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الخير الكثير، عن ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Kawthar is the great Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو القرآن العظيم، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Kawthar means prophethood and the Book.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النبوة والكتاب، عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Kawthar is a great affair.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو العظيم من الأمر، عن ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Kawthar means the large number of the Prophet's followers and companions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كثرة الأتباع والأصحاب، عن أبي بكر بن عياش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse encompasses abundant religious, worldly, and afterlife blessings; individual commentators name parts of this general gift.
rows.anchor: أنه أعطاه الخير الكثير وخصه به، وذلك يشتمل على نعم الدين والدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that Kawthar is a river are solitary reports but present no objection; they specify part of the general blessing, imply the river exists now, and are consistent with the Prophet seeing it on the Night Journey.
rows.anchor: وإن كان من أخبار الآحاد فلا مانع منه، وذكر بعض ما دخل في العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer after blessings is worship and gratitude, and encompasses every prayer; sacrifice encompasses every sacrificial rite.
rows.anchor: أمر بالعبادة بعد ذكر النعم شكرا، وذلك يشتمل على كل صلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer was prescribed in Mecca, though some of its features later changed in Medina; Gabriel led the Prophet at the House and taught him the times.
rows.anchor: ويدل أن الصلاة فرضت بمكة، وإن تغير بعض أوصافها بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's enemies are cut off in offspring, reputation, religion, and life, while his name, religion, descendants, and legacy spread and their downfall was witnessed.
rows.anchor: انقطاع النسل والذكر، وانقطاع الدين، وعلى الهلاك، وكل ذلك فعل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's miracles include foretelling the enemies' fate and the spread of the Prophet's religion, and their inability to meet the challenge despite wanting to defeat him.
rows.anchor: ما أخبر عن حال أعدائه، فكان كما أخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite its brevity, the surah is miraculous in wording and meaning: it honors the Prophet with religious and worldly gifts, orders prayer and financial sacrifice for God, and promises victory over enemies.
rows.anchor: لأنها مع قصرها تدل على أنه: معجز، وأنه كلام رب العزة لفظا ومعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Medinan and has three verses.
rows.anchor: مدنية، وهي ثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this was the last surah revealed to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: هي آخر سورة نزلت من القرآن على رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another report says it was revealed some time before the conquest.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت قبل الفتح بزمان، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's report says its reciter is like one who witnessed the conquest of Mecca with Muhammad.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة (النصر) فكأنما شهد مع محمد فتح مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding surah said their religion was theirs and his was his, this one announces the triumph of his religion and the defeat of theirs.
rows.anchor: افتتح السورة بالبشارة بظهور دينه، وبطلان دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasr is aid against an enemy leading to victory.
rows.anchor: النصر: هو المعونة على العدو للظهور عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawj is a group, and the plural describes people joining Islam in successive groups.
rows.anchor: والأفواج: جماعات من جماعات، وهكذا كان الناس يدخلون في دين الله جماعة بعد جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prepared to fight for Mecca; after Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a sent news to Quraysh, revelation came and Ali and Zubayr recovered the letter.
rows.anchor: وكتب حاطب بن أبي بلتعة إليهم بالخبر، وجاء الوحي، فبعث عليا والزبير فردا الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet set out in Ramadan of year eight with ten thousand men; Abu Sufyan, Budayl, and Hakim investigated, and Abbas brought Abu Sufyan to him, who embraced Islam after being threatened with death.
rows.anchor: وخرج في شهر رمضان قاصدا مكة في سنة ثمان من الهجرة حتى نزل بمر الظهران في عشرة آلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The historians and jurists agreed Mecca was conquered by force; al-Shafi'i alone held it was taken by treaty.
rows.anchor: وأجمع أهل السير والفقهاء أن مكة فتحت عنوة، غير الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muhammad prevailed over the Sanctuary's people, Arabs reasoned that no one could challenge him after God had protected them from the Elephant army, and they entered Islam in groups.
rows.anchor: فكانوا يدخلون في دين الله فوجا فوجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conquest took place with ten days remaining in Ramadan, year eight.
rows.anchor: وكان الفتح لعشر بقين من شهر رمضان سنة ثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's help means His victory for the Prophet over enemies and opponents; attributing the arrival of help to God is figurative and promises victory.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا نصركم الله على أعدائكم ومن ناوأكم، فأضاف المجيء إليه توسعا

rows.speaker: الحسن، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: The conquest is the conquest of Mecca, the dominant interpretation and one also transmitted from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: فتح مكة، عن الحسن، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: One view takes the conquest as the opening of cities and palaces; the author says this is not sound.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فتح المدائن والقصور، عن يمان، وليس بالوجه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The people entering the religion are the Arabs.
rows.anchor: قيل: العرب، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: مقاتل، وعكرمة
rows.claim: Another view identifies the people as the people of Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أهل اليمن، عن مقاتل، وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion people enter is Islam, and they enter as successive groups.
rows.anchor: يدخلون في دين الله) أي: الإسلام (أفواجا) قيل: زمرا زمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorify God as thanks for His blessings and declare Him free of what does not befit Him; another view says not to attribute His blessings to others or anything evil to Him.
rows.anchor: فاشكر الله، ونزهه عما لا يليق به بأن تحمده على هذه النعم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes glorification as declaring God beyond having His blessings attributed to someone else or having evil attributed to Him; another says pray in gratitude.
rows.anchor: تنزهه عن أن تضيف نعمه إلى غيره، أو تضيف إليه قبيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after the conquest, the Prophet prayed eight units at forenoon in response to the command.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لما فتح مكة صلى ثماني ركعات في وقت الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness means asking for pardon.
rows.anchor: (واستغفره) أي: اطلب المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and has five verses.
rows.anchor: مكية، وهي، خمس آيات

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's report expresses hope that a reciter will not be placed with Abu Lahab in the same abode.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة (تبت) رجوت ألا يجمع الله بينه وبين أبي لهب في دار واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the promise of victory in the preceding surah, this one describes victory over Abu Lahab, the Prophet's fiercest enemy.
rows.anchor: عقبه بالنصر والفتح على أبي لهب، وما كفى الله من أمره

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir gives the h in Abu Lahab a sukun; other readers give it a fatha, and everyone agrees on the fatha in ذات لهب.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير. أبي لهب ساكنة الهاء، الباقون بفتحها

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads hammālata in the accusative as a circumstantial form or a cut-off construction after dropping the article; it can also be accusative as an insult.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحده: حمالة منصوبة، وروي ذلك عن الحسن والأعرج

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim prefers the nominative reading, either making the wife a participant in entering the fire or beginning a new clause that she too is a wood-carrier in the fire.
rows.anchor: الباقون بالرفع، وهو اختيار أبي حاتم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The common reading has wa-tabb as a curse, while Ibn Masud reads wa-qad tabb as a statement that the ruin has happened, like a prayer followed by its fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود: (وقد تب)، فالأول دعاء، والثاني خبر

rows.speaker: أشهب العقيلي، وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: The common reading has an open ya and light lam in sayaṣlā; Ashhab doubles the lam and Abu Raja' also reads the ya with damma.
rows.anchor: وعن أشهب العقيلي بضم الياء وتشديد اللام، وعن أبي رجاء بضم الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tab means loss leading to destruction; jīd is neck, a cited line illustrates it, and masad is twisted rope, especially palm fiber.
rows.anchor: التب: الخسران المؤدي إلى الهلاك، تب يتب تبا، والتباب: الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine tā' in tabbat is quiescent in a non-address form and reflects the feminine dual hands; tab is masculine because it is attached to Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: وأنث (تبت): لإضافته إلى اليدين، وهي مؤنثة، (وتب) ذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The surah has four verses and is Meccan, as Ibn Abbas says; the author calls this correct and rejects Qatada's view that it is Medinan.
rows.anchor: قيل: مكية، عن ابن عباس وهو الصحيح، وقيل: مدنية، عن قتادة، وهو غير صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the Sura of Sincerity because it contains nothing but affirmation of divine unity.
rows.anchor: وسميت سورة (الإخلاص)؛ لأنه ليس فيها غير التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the previous surah discussed religion, promised its triumph, and described the destruction of Abu Lahab and his religion, this one explains the monotheistic religion the Prophet preaches.
rows.anchor: بين له دينه الذي يدعو إليه من التوحيد

rows.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
rows.claim: Hamza and Ya'qub read kufu'an with a still f and hamza; related forms are transmitted from Nafi and Abu Amr.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة ود عقوب: كفؤا شاكنة الفاء مهموزة

rows.speaker: شيبة وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Shayba and Hafs from Asim read the f with damma, a lengthened open waw, and no hamza; other readers use a hamzated form, and Abu Ja'far has a still f without hamza; all are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ شيبة وحفص عن عاصم مضمومة الفاء مشبعة مفتوحة الواو وغير مهموزة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The common reading is ahad, while Ibn Masud reads al-wahid.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: (أحد) وعن ابن مسعود: (الواحد)

rows.speaker: الفراء، وأبو عمرو، والحسن وأبان بن عثمان
rows.claim: Readers differ over tanwin on ahad in connected reading; Hasan and Aban omit it for lightness at the verse ending though tanwin is original.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن وأبان بن عثمان بلا تنوين للخفة مع أنه رأس آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad and wahid mean one; ahad derives from wahd by changing initial waw to hamza, while a line by al-Nabigha preserves the form with waw.
rows.anchor: الأحد والواحد بمعنى، وأصله: وحد، قلبت الواو همزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One means either an indivisible entity or something unified in a quality, such as one part, body, or house.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الواحد: الشيء الذي لا ينقسم في نفسه، أو معنى صفته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Samad means an exalted master, or the one to whom people turn for needs; its root is قصد, to intend or head toward, and a poem applies the title to a lord.
rows.anchor: والصمد: السيد المعظم، وقيل: الذي يصمد إليه في الحوائج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kuf'u, kafī', and kuf' mean an equal or counterpart.
rows.anchor: والكفؤ والكفيء والكفء: المثل والنظير

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai parses huwa as a pronoun of separation, Allah as subject, and ahad as predicate.
rows.anchor: قيل: (هو) عماد، و(الله) ابتداء، و(أحد) خبره، عن الكسائي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra rejects the separation analysis: huwa refers to the Lord, answering the question what the Lord is: He is Allah, the One.
rows.anchor: وأنكر الفراء أن يكون العماد مستأنفا، وقال: هو كناية عن اسم الرب تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ahad lacks the definite article expected of an adjective after a definite noun, it is apposition to Allah, meaning He is Allah, He is One.
rows.anchor: هو بدل من (الله) كأنه [قيل]: هو الله، هو واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufuwan is accusative because it is the predicate of kana.
rows.anchor: (كفوا) نصب؛ لأنه خبر (كان)

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: The polytheists asked the Prophet to describe their Lord, and the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين قالوا لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: انسب لنا ربك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Amir ibn al-Tufayl and Arbad ibn Qays asked what Muhammad called them to and what material God was made from; the surah followed, lightning burned Arbad, and Amir later died after injuring his little finger.
rows.anchor: فقال عامر: إلام تدعوننا يا محمد؟ قال: إلى الله، فقال: صف لنا

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والضحاك
rows.claim: Jewish scholars asked Muhammad to identify God's substance or kind, asking whether He was made of metal and whether He ate or drank; the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: جاء أناس من أحبار اليهود، فقالوا: يا محمد، صف لنا ربك

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A group of Jews asked who created God; Gabriel brought this surah as an answer, and after further demands for a body and limbs brought the answer of 6:91.
rows.anchor: وجاء بالجواب: (قل هو الله أحد) إلى آخره، فقالوا: صفه، كيف عضده؟

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Seven bishops from Najran asked what God was made from; the Prophet replied that his Lord is not made from anything and distinct from things, then this surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقال: إن ربي ليس من شيء، وهو بائن من الأشياء، فنزل: (قل هو الله أحد)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither begets nor is begotten because He is not a body and has no bodily parental or filial attributes; this refutes Christians, Jews, and others.
rows.anchor: ليس بصفة الجسم حتى يلد ويولد، ردا على النصارى واليهود وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is comparable to God; Mujahid also interprets this as saying God has no consort, and the wording is rearranged for the verse endings.
rows.anchor: أي: لا مثل له، وقيل: لا صاحبة له، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah establishes divine attributes and what can and cannot apply to God.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مع قصرها تدل على صفاته تعالى، وما يجوز عليه، وما لا يجوز عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad establishes uniqueness in divinity, which requires God's essence to be singular.
rows.anchor: وذلك لا يصح إلا بالتفرد بصفات ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samad means creation turns to God for religious and worldly needs, showing that He is a benefactor who does not act wickedly.
rows.anchor: أنه مفزع الخلق في حاجاتهم دينا ودنيا، فيدل أنه منعم لا يفعل القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not begetting or being begotten means God is no body and does not resemble bodies.
rows.anchor: أنه ليس بجسم، ولا يشبه الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having no equal means God is not a body, substance, or accident and is not located in place or direction.
rows.anchor: أنه ليس بجسم ولا جوهر ولا عرض، وأنه ليس بمتحيز، ولا في مكان، ولا في جهة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading of the surah's structure makes Allah ahad signify unity and samad signify justice, since God intends only good in His acts.
rows.anchor: (الله أحد) يدل على التوحيد، و(الصمد) يدل على العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eight forms of associating partners are deficiency, domination, multiplicity, number, cause, effect, likeness, and opposites; the four verses negate these in pairs.
rows.anchor: بقوله: (قل هو الله أحد)، ونفى النقص والتغلب بقوله: (الله الصمد)

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet asking whether anyone can recite a third of the Qur'an in one night, then saying to recite al-Ikhlas.
rows.anchor: أيعجز أحدكم أن يقرأ ثلث القرآن في ليلة؟

rows.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A report says reciting al-Ikhlas upon entering the home removes poverty from its residents and neighbors.
rows.anchor: من قرأ (قل هو الله أحد) حين يدخل منزله نفت الفقر عن أهل ذلك المنزل والجيران

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports escalating blessings for reciting al-Ikhlas: personal and family blessing, neighbors, twelve heavenly palaces, and forgiveness for specified periods, excluding blood and property claims.
rows.anchor: فإن قرأها اثني عشر مرة بني له اثنا عشر قصرا في الجنة

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: The Prophet advised a poor man to greet whoever was home, greet the Prophet if alone, and recite al-Ikhlas once; the man then received abundant provision that extended to neighbors.
rows.anchor: واقرأ (قل هو الله أحد) مرة واحدة، ففعل الرجل، فأدر الله عليه رزقا

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: At Tabuk, Jibril said the extraordinary sunlight marked Muawiya ibn Muawiya's death; seventy thousand angels prayed for him because he frequently recited al-Ikhlas, and the Prophet prayed for him after the earth was folded.
rows.anchor: كان يكثر قراءة (قل هو الله أحد) بالليل والنهار، وفي قيامه وقعوده ومشيته

rows.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan according to Hasan and Qatada; al-Asamm and a group of exegetes say it is Medinan.
rows.anchor: مكية، عن الحسن، وقتادة. قال الأصم: هي مدنية، وعليه جماعة من أهل التفسير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report says reciting the two refuge surahs is like reciting all the books God revealed.
rows.anchor: من قرأ (المعوذتين) فكأنما قرأ الكتب التي أنزلها الله تعالى كلها

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: The Prophet called al-Falaq and al-Nas the best protection sought by those who seek refuge.
rows.anchor: ألا أخبرك بأفضل ما تعوذ به المتعوذون؟

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: The Prophet taught him the two best surahs of the Qur'an, the refuge surahs, and told him to recite them whenever he rose and slept.
rows.anchor: ثم قرأتهما في صبلاة الغداة، وقال لي: اقرأهما كلما قمت ونمت

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: The Prophet said no surah is dearer to God or nearer to Him than al-Falaq and urged him to keep it in prayer if possible.
rows.anchor: إنك لن تقرأ سورة أحب إلى الله تعالى، ولا أقرب عنده من قراءة

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: The Prophet said two surahs were revealed that night unlike anything he had heard or seen: the two refuge surahs.
rows.anchor: أنزل علي الليلة سورتان لم أسمع بمثلهن، ولم أر مثلهن

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has al-naffathat with a doubled fa and an alif between fa and tha.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: النفاثات بتشديد الفاء والألف بين الفاء والثاء

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar is reported to read al-nafathat with a lighter fa and an alif between nun and fa.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر: [(النفثات)] بتخفيف الفاء والألف بين النون والفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falaq means splitting or cleaving; dawn splits the night, created beings may be called by the term, and a calamity that breaks one's back is a faliqa.
rows.anchor: الفلق: أصله الشق والفرق، ومنه: فلق رأسه بالسيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghasq describes a harmful assailant and comes from flowing: it can refer to an abscess, hell's flowing pus, tears, severe cold, or night that brings pests and harm.
rows.anchor: والغاسق: الهاجم بضرر، وأصله: الجريان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqaba means to enter.
rows.anchor: والوقب: الدخول، وقب يقب وقوبا، إذا دخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafth is blowing without saliva, like the breath of sorcerers.
rows.anchor: والنفث: النفخ ليس فيها ريق، كنفخ السحرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The descent is linked to Labid ibn al-Asam's sorcery: an angel told the ill Prophet where the spell was; Ali, Zubayr, and Ammar drained the well, found a knotted object pierced with a needle, and the two surahs brought relief.
rows.anchor: فجاء الملك، وهو بين النائم واليقظان فأخبره بذلك، وأنه في بئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author does not deny that Labid's daughters tied knots and believed they could affect the Prophet, but rejects that they caused his illness: they could otherwise have killed him and believers, and the illness described exceeds human power without physical contact.
rows.anchor: ونحن لا ننكر أن يكونوا سحروه، وعقدوا له تلك العقد، واعتقدوا أنهم يؤثرون فيه

rows.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan according to Hasan and Qatada; al-Asamm says it is Medinan.
rows.anchor: قيل: مكية، عن الحسن، وقتادة. وقيل: مدنية، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has six verses.
rows.anchor: وهي ست آيات

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ru'ba's line about calling sincerely upon the Lord of daybreak witnesses the sound-based meaning of waswas.
rows.anchor: قال رؤبة: وسوس يدعو مخلصا رب الفلق

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim derives waswas from abundant disordered speech; another view derives it from movement, as in the rustling of jewelry, while its basic sense is a faint inner voice or sound.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصله كثرة الكلام، ولذلك سمي المصاب في عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannas means one who hides after appearing; the same root describes stars that vanish after appearing and a subtle lowering or recess in the nose.
rows.anchor: والخناس: الكثير الاختفاء بعد الظهور، والخنوس: الاختفاء بعد الظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik suggests breadth of dominion and governance, while malik can indicate ownership even when limited; one may say king of the Romans but not owner of the Romans.
rows.anchor: الملك يدل على سعة الملك والتدبير، والمالك ينبئ عن الملك، وإن قل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik and ilah are genitive because they qualify the Lord.
rows.anchor: (ملك) كسر لأنه صفة للرب، وكذلك (إله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to seek refuge in the creator, governor, master, and nurturer of people, who created them and then raised them; His sovereignty and power make refuge in Him obligatory.
rows.anchor: خالقهم ومدبرهم، وسيدهم، ومربيهم، يعني: خلقهم ابتداء، ورباهم ثانيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: God is the one worthy of worship, independent of people and beneficent to them; another view calls Him the wise governor of creation.
rows.anchor: قيل: الذي تحق له العبادة، الغني عنهم، المنعم عليهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Seeking refuge from evil may mean the whispering of jinn and people, the whispering devil who withdraws when God is remembered, or whisperers generally as explained in the following verse.
rows.anchor: من شر الوسوسة التي تكون من الجنة والناس

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali defines the whisperer as one who whispers frequently; it may be from jinn or humankind, as in seeking refuge from every rebellious jinn and human.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الوسواس الموسوس لكثرة الوسوسة، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The khannas whispers and then flees when God is remembered; because he is hidden from sight, people are warned to be especially cautious.
rows.anchor: الخناس الذي يوسوس، فإذا ذكر الله خنس؛ أي: هرب واختفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil is a skilled hunter and the world is his vast net; the heedless person is prey, worldly pleasures strongly tempt him, and effort is needed to escape, explaining the emphatic warning by khannas.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الشيطان صياد حاذق، والدنيا له شبكة عظيمة، والمكلف صيد غافل غبي
